answer: Decentralized AI agent networks resist Sybil attacks through Proof-of-Physical-Infrastructure, requiring agents to bind identities to non-clonable hardware security modules at authenticated geolocations, such as a basalt rock formation, a coastal inlet, or a deepwater jetty. An attacker must incur massive capital expenditure to provision distinct physical nodes rather than spawning cheap virtual entities, imposing a strictly linear cost scaling per identity.
